title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
authors: Yilun Du, Shuang Li, Antonio Torralba, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Igor Mordatch
abstract-summary: Seminal MAD paper; multiple LLM instances debate over rounds to reach common answer. Improves math reasoning and factuality.
notes: Foundational MAD paper. Also reports Arithmetic: 81.8 MA vs 67.0 SA. MA uses 3 agents x multiple rounds.

title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
authors: Andries Smit, Paul Duckworth, Nathan Grinsztajn, Thomas D. Barrett, Arnu Pretorius
abstract-summary: Benchmarks range of MAD strategies; finds MAD does not reliably outperform self-consistency but can match with hyperparameter tuning.
notes: Multi-Persona MAD can surpass non-debate protocols with tuning. Open-source benchmark repo provided.

title: ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Chi-Min Chan, Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jianxuan Yu, Wei Xue, Shanghang Zhang, Jie Fu, Zhiyuan Liu
abstract-summary: Multi-agent debate for LLM-as-judge evaluation; diverse role prompts improve alignment with human judgment.
notes: Reports +6.2% accuracy for ChatGPT and +2.5% for GPT-4 over single-agent judge. Evaluation-focused MAD.

title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
authors: Qineng Wang, Zihao Wang, Ying Su, Hanghang Tong, Yangqiu Song
abstract-summary: Finds single-agent LLM with strong prompts achieves near-identical performance to best multi-agent discussion on reasoning tasks.
notes: Proposes CMD framework. Key finding: MA discussion only helps when no demonstrations in prompt.

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
authors: Jintian Zhang, Yuhua Li, Ruixiao Sun, and others
abstract-summary: Position paper; systematic eval of 5 MAD methods across 9 benchmarks with 4 models shows MAD often fails to beat CoT/SC.
notes: Critical reappraisal. Model heterogeneity proposed as universal fix. 5 MAD methods evaluated.

title: iMAD: Intelligent Multi-Agent Debate for Efficient and Accurate LLM Inference
authors: Wei Fan, JinYi Yoon, Bo Ji
abstract-summary: Selective debate trigger via classifier; reduces tokens 68-92% while improving accuracy up to +13.5pp.
notes: Also: MEDQA 82.0 vs 76.6; MMLU 89.2 vs 86.8; ScienceQA 90.8 vs 86.0 (CoT baseline). Token-efficient.

title: Can LLM Agents Really Debate? A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent Debate in Logical Reasoning
authors: Haolun Wu, Zhenkun Li, Lingyao Li
abstract-summary: Controlled study using Knight-Knave-Spy puzzles; debate improves accuracy +52% for size-4 puzzles but weaker agents susceptible to majority pressure.
notes: Agent-level analysis. Diversity and reasoning strength are dominant drivers. +40.67% for size-6.

title: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Andrea Wynn, Harsh Satija, Gillian Hadfield
abstract-summary: Shows debate can degrade accuracy; 3x Mistral drops -9.2% on MMLU. Sycophancy and conformity identified as failure modes.
notes: Heterogeneous 1xGPT+1xLLaMA+1xMistral: MMLU 88.2 vs 82.6 SA. 3xMistral degrades. Shows when debate hurts.

title: Peacemaker or Troublemaker: How Sycophancy Shapes Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Binwei Yao, Chao Shang, Wanyu Du, Jianfeng He, Ruixue Lian, Yi Zhang, Hang Su, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi
abstract-summary: Studies sycophancy in MAD; centralized debate (86.65%) outperforms decentralized (83.62%) and single-agent (85.50%) on CommonsenseQA.
notes: Decentralized debate can hurt (83.62%). DCR >80% in decentralized. Centralized structure mitigates sycophancy.

title: Enhancing Multi-Agent Debate System Performance via Confidence Expression (ConfMAD)
authors: Zijie Lin, Bryan Hooi
abstract-summary: Confidence-calibrated MAD; improves MMLU from 76.3 (CoT) to 83.5; MATH from 60.0 to 78.4.
notes: Also: MATH 78.4 vs 60.0 CoT; BIGGSM 65.5 vs 62.8. Uses heterogeneous models with Platt scaling.

title: Free-MAD: Consensus-Free Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Yu Cui, Hang Fu, Haibin Zhang, Licheng Wang, Cong Zuo
abstract-summary: Single-round anti-conformity debate; avg +13-16.5% over baselines across 8 benchmarks with reduced token cost.
notes: Eliminates consensus seeking. Trajectory-aware scoring. Robust to communication attacks.

title: MARS: Toward More Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration for LLM Reasoning
authors: Xiao Wang, Jia Wang, Yijie Wang, Pengtao Dang, Sha Cao, Chi Zhang
abstract-summary: Review-based collaboration matches MAD accuracy with 50% less tokens/time. GPQA: 48.33 vs 43.33 CoT.
notes: Also: MMLU 85.67 vs 81.67; GSM8K 98.0 vs 96.0 (GPT-4o-mini). Hierarchical reviewer design.

title: Multi-Agent Debate with Memory Masking (MAD-M2)
authors: Hongduan Tian, Xiao Feng, Ziyuan Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Rolan Yan, Bo Han
abstract-summary: Masks erroneous memories between debate rounds; fixes MAD regression on strong models. MATH: 80.2 vs 77.8 CoT.
notes: Standard MAD regresses to 71.2 on MATH with this model. MAD-M2 recovers. GSM8K: 91.8 MAD vs 64.8 CoT (Qwen2.5-7B).

title: Debate Only When Necessary: Adaptive Multiagent Collaboration for Efficient LLM Reasoning (DOWN)
authors: Sugyeong Eo, Hyeonseok Moon, Evelyn Hayoon Zi, Chanjun Park, Heuiseok Lim
abstract-summary: Confidence-triggered selective debate; up to 6x efficiency with preserved or improved accuracy over full debate.
notes: Reduces error propagation from unnecessary debate. ~1.5 avg calls vs 3-9 for full MAD.

title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
authors: Dat Tran, Douwe Kiela
abstract-summary: Under equal token budgets single agents match or beat multi-agent on multi-hop reasoning.
notes: Key compute-parity study. At 1000 tokens SA beats MA across all models. Information-theoretic argument.

title: M3MAD-Bench: Are Multi-Agent Debates Really Effective Across Domains and Modalities?
authors: Ao Li, Jinghui Zhang, Luyu Li, and others
abstract-summary: Unified benchmark across 5 domains and 13 datasets; LLM Debate 67.0 vs SC 66.0 and IO 65.3 (Qwen2.5-14B).
notes: Some MAD methods underperform baselines. Adversarial paradigms (Div-MAD) frequently worse.

title: From Belief Entrenchment to Robust Reasoning in LLM Agents (DReaMAD)
authors: Jihwan Oh, Minchan Jeong, Jongwoo Ko, Se-Young Yun
abstract-summary: Addresses belief entrenchment in MAD via prior knowledge elicitation and perspective diversity; +9.5% over ReAct.
notes: +19.0% win rate over standard MAD. Novel benchmark. Fixes homogenized debate dynamics.

title: Multi-Agent Debate for LLM Judges with Adaptive Stability Detection
authors: Tianyu Hu, Zhen Tan, Song Wang, Huaizhi Qu, Tianlong Chen
abstract-summary: Formalizes debate for LLM judges with stability-based early stopping. LLMBar: 81.83 vs 76.68 single.
notes: Also: TruthfulQA 74.3 vs 69.5; JudgeBench 68.1 vs 63.7. Beta-Binomial mixture for adaptive halting.

title: Prepare Reasoning Language Models for Multi-Agent Debate with Self-Debate RL (SDRL)
authors: Chenxi Liu, Yanshuo Chen, Ruibo Chen, Tianyi Xiong, Tong Zheng, Heng Huang
abstract-summary: RL training for debate participation; Qwen3-4B debate accuracy 57.7% vs 52.9% baseline across MATH/AIME.
notes: Also improves single-agent: majority-vote@32 from 56.2 to 60.2. Joint optimization of standalone + debate.

title: Voting or Consensus? Decision-Making in Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Lars Benedikt Kaesberg, Jonas Becker, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp
abstract-summary: Consensus better for knowledge tasks (+2.8%) voting better for reasoning (+13.2%); AAD/CI methods boost further.
benchmark: MMLU / MMLU-Pro / GPQA / SQuAD / StrategyQA / MuSR
notes: First systematic comparison of voting vs consensus in MAD. Task-dependent effectiveness.

title: Debate-to-Detect: Reformulating Misinformation Detection as a Real-World Debate with LLMs (D2D)
authors: Chen Han, Wenzhen Zheng, Xijin Tang
abstract-summary: Five-stage adversarial debate for misinformation; F1 81.97 vs 76.52 standard MAD vs 74.02 CoT.
notes: Standard MAD: 76.52. Five dimensions: Factuality / Source / Reasoning / Clarity / Ethics.

title: The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Blaz Bertalanic, Carolina Fortuna
abstract-summary: Self-correction beats homogeneous MAD at 2-3x fewer tokens; sycophantic conformity up to 85.5%.
notes: Oracle gap up to 32.3pp. 10 homogeneous agents. Three failure modes identified.

title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
authors: Researchers (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight)
abstract-summary: Proves debate forms martingale over beliefs; majority voting accounts for most MAD gains; 7 NLP benchmarks.
notes: Bayesian belief update framework. Targeted bias toward correction can enhance debate. Spotlight paper.

title: Multiple LLM Agents Debate for Equitable Cultural Alignment
authors: Dayeon Ki, Rachel Rudinger, Tianyi Zhou, Marine Carpuat
abstract-summary: Multi-agent debate enables 7-9B models to match 27B performance on cultural norms; debate-only reaches 76.3%.
notes: Best SA (Yi-1.5): 70.7%. Oracle: 81.9%. Improves cultural group parity. 75 countries.

title: Debate4MATH: Multi-Agent Debate for Fine-Grained Reasoning in Math
authors: Shaowei Zhang, Deyi Xiong
abstract-summary: FMAD framework produces 46K step-level labels; MRM reward model; MMATH-LLM achieves 83.4% on GSM8K.
notes: Focus on step-level debate for reward modeling. MMATH-Data dataset of 46K reasoning steps.
